note: Applies to any asset whose manifest sets is_growable: true. A growth group is a normal asset (own folder, own manifest, own category) that additionally owns a growth scheme and a pool of stage resources. The GROUP is authoritative: the scheme (growth_type, max_age, time_unit, stages[]) lives here and nowhere else. Stage folders under stages/ are resources the scheme selects from - they are NOT catalog assets themselves and are never walked by build_full_catalog(). This replaces the older design where every stage item carried its own full duplicate of the shared stages[] array (see kit_config.json growth_groups, retained only for migration).
note_authority: The ASSET is the authoritative answer for itself. A group's scheme (growth_type, max_age, time_unit, stages[]) is owned by this manifest and nowhere else. kit_config.json growth_groups was only the one-time migration SOURCE for this data - it is not read at runtime and its per-species entries are removed once migrated, so the two can never drift. Per-stage manifests and generated READMEs are likewise not authoritative for the scheme; only this file is.

is_growable.note: TOP-LEVEL on the asset manifest, not inside the growth block. This is the flag that marks the asset itself as a growth group: it is what makes the growth block mandatory and what makes stages/ meaningful. Deliberately at the root so a generic tool can test manifest.is_growable without knowing the growth block's shape. An asset without it is an ordinary item. Never duplicate this inside growth.

growth_type.note: Broad lifecycle class. Drives which default rules apply (e.g. whether the group is placeable, harvestable at maturity, rideable). 'generic' is the fallback for anything not clearly tree/crop/animal. 'percent' is the CONSTRUCTION lifecycle (all nine assets/structures groups): it does not advance on its own with time - it advances as the player contributes materials and labour (see each stage manifest's category_fields.construction_recipe and required_tools), so its stages are construction phases (foundation -> framing -> walls -> complete) rather than ages. Because progress is a fraction of a finished build rather than a duration, the scheme is expressed as a percentage of completion: max_age is fixed at 100 and time_unit is 'percent', so each stage claims a band of the build (foundation 0-33, framing 33-66, walls 66-99, complete 99-100).

species.note: Stable species key for this group, matching the group folder id (e.g. 'oak'). Used for lookups and for cross-referencing from other systems (harvest yields, spawning rules). Must be unique across all categories.

max_age.note: Total lifespan in time_unit. The final stage's age_max must equal this value, so a group is fully grown exactly at max_age. For growth_type 'percent' this is always 100 - the build is complete at 100% - so it is a fixed consequence of the class rather than a per-group choice.

time_unit.note: Unit for all ages in this scheme (age_min, age_max, max_age). 'days' is the norm for trees/crops/animals. For growth_type 'percent' it is always 'percent' - the two go together, and max_age is always 100. The usual 'age' semantics still hold - age_min/age_max stay contiguous and ascending, and the final stage's age_max must still equal max_age - so 'percent' is a relabelling of the same numeric axis (0..100 instead of 0..N days), not a different shape.

total_stages.note: Must equal the length of stages[]. Redundant by design - a cheap integrity check that catches a truncated or hand-edited stages array.

stages.note: Ordered lifecycle. Each entry selects ONE resource folder from the group's own stages/ directory. Contiguous, non-overlapping, ascending: stages[0].age_min must be 0, each entry's age_max must equal the next entry's age_min, and the last entry's age_max must equal max_age. The STAGE does not own growth data - it is a pointer into the scheme plus a resource selection.

stage.note: 1-based position in the lifecycle. Stage 1 is the youngest (seed/sapling/foal/egg).

name.note: Human-readable stage name used by the UI and by generated READMEs (e.g. 'sapling', 'small', 'medium', 'mature').

age_min.note: Inclusive lower age bound in time_unit.

age_max.note: Exclusive upper age bound in time_unit. Must be greater than age_min.

sexes.note: ANIMALS ONLY. The female / male choice, part of the stage it happens at (normally the final stage: baby and yearling are sexless). When an animal reaches the stage it becomes ONE of these at random, by `chance_pct` (female 80 / male 20 is the norm; the chances add up to 100). The models live in the stage's own resource folder, next to the stage model. Without `sexes` every animal becomes the stage as it is. Runtime: GrowthStage.Sexes / GrowthStage.PickSex in Assets/Scripts/Growth/GrowthGroup.cs.

chance_pct.note: Chance (percent) that an animal reaching the stage becomes this sex.

model.note: Model filename inside the stage's resource folder.

icon.note: Icon filename inside the stage's resource folder.

construction_recipe.note: STRUCTURES only (growth_type percent): the materials CONSUMED to build this stage, [{item_id, quantity}] where item_id is an item or a #tag; a line may instead be an OR group {

: [{item_id, quantity}, ...]}: any ONE alternative in full (2 x Large 2x4 Bundle OR 4 x Small 2x4 Bundle). Authoritative here; the stage's own manifest copy (category_fields.construction_recipe) is derived. Edited in the stages table of the group's scheme panel with the asset picker.

required_tools.note: STRUCTURES only: tool GROUPS for this stage, each an array of alternative tool ids or #tags (the player needs ANY ONE of each group, in the toolbar or placed near the site; tools are not used up). Authoritative here; the stage manifest copy is derived.

resource.note: Relative path to this stage's resource folder, always of the form 'stages/<folder>/'. The folder holds that stage's manifest, model files, icon, and materials. Relative to the group's own folder, which keeps OBJ/MTL internal references valid and makes migration a folder move rather than a file rewrite.

model.note: Model filename within the stage's resource folder (e.g. 'SM_Tree_Oak_Small.fbx'). Resolved as <resource>/<model>. This is the field the runtime reads to decide what to display at this point in the scheme.

icon.note: Optional per-stage icon filename within the stage's resource folder. The GROUP's own icon (the largest stage's icon, copied to the group root) is what the catalog shows; this is only used for stage-level UI.

category_fields.note: Per-stage data that belongs to the STAGE, not the group - declared here so this one file describes the whole group, but stored on the stage's own manifest at <resource>/<stage_id>.json (a stage is a resource, so its manifest is the authority for its own fields). Which keys are expected is decided by the group's CATEGORY schema (assets/_schemas/<category>.schema.json): a structures stage carries interior_area_m2/room_count/electrical_service_capacity_w/water_supply_capacity_lpm/roof_area_m2 plus the per-stage construction_recipe and required_tools; a farming stage carries crop_species/days_to_mature/season/yield_amount/yields_item_id. Deliberately NOT duplicated onto the group manifest, and never merged upward - a 4-stage building has four DIFFERENT construction_recipe/required_tools sets, one per stage, so a single group-level copy could only ever be wrong for three of them.

icon_stage.note: Which stage's icon is promoted to the group's own icon. By convention this is the LARGEST stage (the highest stage number), because the catalog should show the asset at its most recognisable, fully-grown appearance rather than its seed form.

rules.required_when: growth_type in [tree, crop]. These rules apply ONLY to trees and crops - omit the block for animal, percent (construction groups advance by player contribution, not by environment) and generic groups, and a validator should reject it there.
rules.note: The GROUP-LEVEL growth rules. The group OWNS its whole lifecycle - what plants it (planting.item_id), the ingredient it drops (yield.item_id), what harvests it (yield.tool), and its withered (crops) or stump (trees) and dead versions (failure.withered / yield.stump / failure.dead); items carry none of this. everything about HOW and WHEN the group grows and what it yields, as opposed to the scheme (stages/ages) which says WHAT it looks like at each age. Group-authoritative like the scheme - these values live here and nowhere else. Formerly these were duplicated on each stage as farming category_fields (days_to_mature, irrigated_growth_bonus_pct, fertilized_growth_bonus_pct, season, yield_amount, yields_item_id) or lived in game code; stage manifests must NOT repeat them. Growth-speed modifiers are NOT crop rules: how much irrigating or fertilizing speeds growth is a property of the irrigation item (category_fields.irrigated_growth_bonus_pct on water_sprinkler / water_irrigation_sprinkler_riser / water_hose_soaker_flat) or the fertilizer (category_fields.fertilizer_growth_bonus_pct on mat_fertilizer / waste_pile_manure_*). Every sub-block is optional except where noted; a missing sub-block means 'no rule' (no boost, no restriction, cannot fail).

yield.note: What harvesting produces. Only the harvest stage is harvestable; earlier stages never yield. Omit entirely for non-harvestable groups (ornamental trees, wild growth).

item_id.note: The INGREDIENT DROPPED when harvested: a catalog item id - a food_* item directly, or an ingredient_* item needing processing; for TREES a mat_log_* material (the logs a felled tree gives). Must exist in the catalog. A tree's yield also drives the procedural forest: its tool decides what can fell those trees (the ACTIVE toolbar item, right-click), and amount_max is the log count of a mature tree (smaller trees give a fraction).

tools.note: What harvests it: ANY ONE of these works. Empty or omitted = by hand (right-click a ready plant with anything selected). Otherwise the player must have one of them as the ACTIVE toolbar slot when right-clicking a ready plant. Each entry is a real item id (e.g. 'tool_sickle') or a tag written '#tag_name' (any ONE member of the tag from assets/_schemas/material_tags.json works). Every entry must reference an existing item or tag.

tool.note: Legacy single harvest tool; read as a list of one when 'tools' is absent. New data writes 'tools'.

extras.note: MORE THAN ONE YIELD: additional drops given on every harvest, on top of item_id. Each entry is { item_id, amount_min, amount_max } (a catalog item id and a whole-number range, 1 <= amount_min <= amount_max). Requires item_id to be set.

stump.note: TREES ONLY. The STUMP: what is left standing after the tree is harvested (felled), instead of the plant disappearing. Same shape as a stage entry: `resource` ('stages/<folder>/') and `model`, both or neither. Omitted = the harvested tree is simply removed. Ignored for perennials that regrow (yield.regrows), which go back to regrow_stage instead. Crops use failure.withered, not this.

amount_min.note: Fewest units produced per harvest (a whole number).

amount_max.note: Most units produced per harvest (a whole number, >= amount_min). Each harvest rolls a random WHOLE number from amount_min to amount_max INCLUSIVE, so 2..5 can give 2, 3, 4 or 5. Set both the same for a fixed yield.

harvest_stage.note: Stage number at which harvest is allowed. Defaults to the final stage (total_stages).

regrows.note: True for perennials (fruit trees, berry bushes): after harvest the group returns to regrow_stage instead of being removed.

regrow_stage.note: Stage to return to after a harvest when regrows is true. Required if regrows is true; must be less than harvest_stage.

fruit.note: TREES ONLY. PICKING: a fruiting tree can be picked while it stands (the tree is not felled). Picking gives the drops, then the fruit regrows after regrow_days game days. Separate from the yield block, which is the harvest / felling.

is_fruiting.note: True for a fruiting tree. When false the whole block is ignored.

drops.note: What one pick gives: a list of { item_id, amount_min, amount_max } (catalog item ids, whole-number ranges). At least one entry when is_fruiting is true.

tools.note: What picks the fruit: ANY ONE of these in the ACTIVE toolbar slot (an item id, e.g. 'tool_fruit_basket', or a '#tag'). Empty or omitted = by hand. Every entry must reference an existing item or tag.

fruit_stage.note: Stage number from which the tree bears fruit. Defaults to the final stage.

regrow_days.note: Game days until the fruit is back after a pick.

planting.note: Where and when the group can be planted and can grow.

seasons.note: Seasons in which planting is allowed and growth proceeds. 'year_round' (greenhouse-friendly) must appear alone. Omitted = year_round. Replaces the old per-item 'season' string.

item_id.note: The item that PLANTS this group: the seed / sapling the player right-clicks the ground with. The GROUP owns this link - the item carries nothing about it, and one item plants exactly one group (no two groups may name the same item). Must be an existing catalog item. Omitted = nothing plants it (world-placed only).

biomes.note: Biome ids (the id/filename of a biome in assets/biomes/, e.g. 'biome_farmland') where this group is a VALID PLACEMENT - it can only be planted, and will only grow, in these biomes. Omitted or empty = valid in any biome. Every id must exist in assets/biomes/. This is where the group may be PLACED; it is distinct from a spawnable asset's spawning.biomes (where the world generator scatters it).

min_temp_c.note: Growth pauses (or fails, per failure rules) below this temperature in Celsius.

max_temp_c.note: Growth pauses (or fails) above this temperature in Celsius.

indoor_ok.note: True if it can be planted inside a greenhouse, ignoring seasons and outdoor temperature (uses the greenhouse's interior temperature instead).

needs.note: Ongoing care the group requires to keep growing.

water_interval_days.note: Must be watered/irrigated at least once per this many days. Omitted = no watering needed (rain-fed or hardy).

fertilizer_required.note: True if growth stalls without fertilizer (heavy feeders); otherwise fertilizer is only a bonus via boosts.

failure.note: What happens when needs or planting conditions are not met.

out_of_season.note: Behaviour when the current season is not in planting.seasons or the temperature is outside min/max: pause growth, wither, or die immediately.

frost_kills.note: True if a frost event destroys it outright regardless of out_of_season.

drought_days_before_wither.note: Days beyond needs.water_interval_days it can go unwatered before withering. Omitted = withers the day the interval is missed.

withered.note: CROPS ONLY (trees use yield.stump instead). The WITHERED VERSION of the plant, shown while it is withering (out of season with out_of_season 'wither', or drought). Same shape as a stage entry: `resource` ('stages/<folder>/', the folder holding its manifest and model) and `model` (filename inside it). Both or neither. Omitted = the plant keeps showing its current stage while withered.

dead.note: The DEAD VERSION of the plant, shown permanently once it dies (frost, or out_of_season 'die', or wither_behavior 'die'). Same shape as `withered`. Omitted = a dying plant is simply removed.

wither_behavior.note: Result of withering: stall (stop growing until fixed), regress_one_stage, or die (removed, no yield).

directory_layout.note: A growth group owns its resources. Everything below lives under assets/<category>/<species>/.

files.<species>.json: The group manifest - this schema. Owns the scheme.
files.<species>.png: The group's catalog icon - a copy of the icon_stage stage's icon.

folders.stages/<stage_name>/: One folder per stage, holding that stage's manifest, model, icon, and materials. Named by the stage's readable name (e.g. stages/tree_sapling/). These are resources, not assets.

migration_note: Migrating an existing group from kit_config.json growth_groups: create the group folder, move each referenced item folder to stages/<stage_name>/ intact (a folder move, so FBX/MTL/PNG and their internal relative references survive untouched), and write the group manifest from the kit_config.json scheme - which is authoritative over the per-item manifests and the generated READMEs, both of which are known to be stale or drifted. Do NOT merge per-stage properties into the group manifest; per-stage data stays with its stage.
